findings.title: Denial cache prevents newly granted/created resources from becoming accessible until TTL expiry
findings.body: Check returns Allowed:false solely from permDenialCache before consulting fresh DB permissions, and no path clears a denial entry when permissions change or when getIdentityPermissions later refreshes permCache for another request. A user checked before creating/being granted a dashboard or folder (or before a grant propagates) is therefore still denied for the full shortCacheTTL (30s), partially defeating this PR's goal of letting creators immediately fetch newly created resources. Only TTL expiry unblocks them.

findings.title: Denial is cached even when the denial may be caused by a stale folder tree
findings.body: On the DB-recheck path, checkPermission -> checkInheritedPermissions still uses buildFolderTree's folderCache (30s TTL); permissions are refreshed but the folder hierarchy is not. A dashboard in a newly created/moved folder can thus be denied because ancestors are missing from the stale tree, and line 154 then promotes that possibly-stale result into permDenialCache for another TTL, extending the incorrect denial beyond the folder-cache expiry and making it immune to the permission refresh.

findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous and shares the permission-cache key prefix
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates namespace, userUID, action, name and parent with '_' and no escaping/length-prefixing, so distinct tuples such as (name='a_b', parent='c') and (name='a', parent='b_c') produce the same key; Grafana UIDs may contain underscores. A denial for one resource can therefore incorrectly deny a different resource. The key also uses the same 'perm_<uid>_<action>' prefix as userPermCacheKey in the same underlying cache, so crafted/extended components can collide with a permission entry (bool vs map JSON), causing spurious cache misses/corrupt entries.

findings.title: List still returns stale cached permissions with no revalidation
findings.body: List accepts getCachedIdentityPermissions as authoritative whenever present and never re-queries the DB, unlike Check which falls back when the cached set does not contain the requested resource. A newly created dashboard/folder (or newly granted scope) will therefore be omitted from List results until permCache expires, so the PR's stated fix for fetching newly created dashboards/folders does not work for list/fetch-many flows that rely on List.
